symptom.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by at least one manic episode of sufficient intensity to cause marked impairment, often requiring hospitalization, and may include psychotic symptoms such as delusions or hallucinations that are typically mood-congruent. Manic episodes involve a sustained period of abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable mood with increased energy and goal-directed activity, often accompanied by decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, and impaired judgment. The course is usually recurrent, with episodes of mania and, in many patients, major depression, and symptoms may be exacerbated by sleep disruption, psychosocial stressors, or substance use. It is distinguished from schizoaffective or primary psychotic disorders by the temporal relationship between mood episodes and psychosis, and from Bipolar II by the presence of full manic episodes rather than hypomania.

patient.personality: Leslie is a highly organized, competitive young production worker who relies on meticulous planning and structure, yet occasionally channels that intensity into obsessive projects and impulsive hobby splurges.
patient.stressor: Leslie’s episode emerged after a period of escalating pressure at work coincided with her decision to take extra online coursework toward Lean Six Sigma certification while still working full-time on rotating shifts. Determined to prove herself as promotion-ready despite being younger than most colleagues, she began stacking her schedule with overtime, exam preparation, and side projects to “fix” inefficiencies on the production line, cutting back on sleep and rigidly tracking every hour in spreadsheets. What initially felt like a productive, high-achieving phase gradually shifted into an increasingly driven, tense state in which she filled evenings and nights with elaborate process maps, meal-prep marathons, and intricate model-building, becoming more impatient and combative with coworkers and family whenever they questioned her pace or priorities. Over roughly two months, her relentless activity, escalating irritability when interrupted, and inability to disengage from new goals led to serious conflict on the floor, missed safety steps, and academic difficulties; after a shouting match with a supervisor and a near-miss incident at work, HR and her parents insisted she see a psychiatrist because her normally controlled, methodical demeanor had transformed into nonstop, agitated overdrive that was clearly undermining her functioning.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve been stuck in this wired, irritable overdrive for weeks, like I can’t stop doing things and everyone is setting me off.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Lately I’m convinced management has hidden cameras on my line and in my apartment because they know I’ve cracked the perfect system to fix all their bottlenecks and they’re trying to steal my ideas before I can present them and get the promotion I clearly deserve.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: When I’m working late at home I keep hearing my supervisor and the plant manager talking right behind me, commenting on my spreadsheets like, “She’s the one, she’s going to change everything,” even though I’m alone in my room and there’s nobody there when I turn around or check the hallway.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: For weeks I’ve been either riding this intense, almost electric high where I feel unbeatable and on a mission, or snapping at people over nothing—like if my mom asks how I’m doing, I instantly feel attacked and blow up at her for “wasting my time.”

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: It’s like I’m plugged into a power outlet all day and night—I’ll work a full shift, then come home and reorganize my entire room, build these complicated cardboard models of the production line, and still feel too revved up to even sit on the couch for five minutes.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: Once I start talking now I can’t stop—I’ll launch into explaining my ideas about reorganizing the whole plant, then jump to my certification plan and then to meal prep and side hustles, and people at work literally have to cut me off because I’m talking so fast they can’t follow me.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: My brain feels like it has a dozen tabs open and they’re all playing at once—while I’m on the line I’m simultaneously redesigning the workflow, planning a new study schedule, calculating macros for meal prep, and replaying arguments with my boss, and I can’t slow any of it down enough to focus on one thing.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: I’ve been cramming every minute with something—picking up extra shifts, signing up for more online modules than I can realistically finish, messaging coworkers at all hours with “solutions,” and pacing the apartment at 3 a.m. because even when there’s nothing left to actually do I still feel driven to keep going.
